text: Nexus University Academic Regulations
title: 01 Academic Regulations

text: Nexus University publishes these Academic Regulations for undergraduate and postgraduate programmes offered on the main campus. They bind every registered student unless a programme-specific handbook states a narrower rule that has been approved by the Academic Council. Where a programme handbook is silent, this document controls. Students are expected to read this file together with attendance, examination, fee, hostel, discipline, and scholarship policies.
title: Academic Year 2026-2027

text:
These regulations apply to all credit-bearing courses taught during Academic Year 2026-27, including summer term courses that carry credit toward a Nexus University award. Guest workshops that do not carry credit are excluded. The Academic Council is the final academic authority. The Registrar maintains the official student record. Faculties may issue operational circulars, but a circular cannot create a new degree requirement unless the Academic Council ratifies it. Students who enrol after the start of a semester remain bound by the regulations in force on the date of enrolment.

The University distinguishes between academic rules, which concern teaching and assessment, and administrative rules, which concern fees, identity, and campus services. Academic rules in this file take precedence over informal advice given by peers, social media posts, or unofficial summaries. Only written communication from the Registrar, Dean, or Controller of Examinations constitutes official academic notice.
title: Scope and Authority

text: In these regulations, "student" means a person whose name appears on the current enrolment roll. "Programme" means a structured set of courses leading to a named award. "Course" means a unit of teaching with a unique course code. "Semester" means the odd term beginning in July or the even term beginning in January, as published in the academic calendar. "Internal assessment" means marks awarded for work completed before the end-semester examination. "Working day" excludes University holidays listed in the calendar. "Identity card" means the official Nexus University smart card issued by the Office of Student Services.
title: Definitions

text: The Academic Calendar for 2026-2027 is published on the student portal not later than 15 May 2026. Course registration opens ten working days before instruction begins and closes on the Friday of the second teaching week. Late registration, if permitted by the Head of Department, attracts the late-registration fee published in the Fee Policy. Students who fail to register by the close of week three are treated as not enrolled for that semester and may not attend classes or sit examinations. Add-and-drop is allowed only during the first two teaching weeks. After that window, withdrawal from a course is recorded as W on the transcript if completed before the mid-semester test, or as F if attempted later without approved medical or academic leave.
title: Academic Calendar and Registration

text: The standard duration of a four-year undergraduate programme is eight semesters. The maximum duration is twelve semesters from first enrolment, after which the student is discontinued unless the Academic Council grants an exceptional extension for documented medical or military service reasons. A full-time undergraduate student shall register for not fewer than sixteen and not more than twenty-six credits in a regular semester. Overload above twenty-six credits requires a cumulative grade point average of at least 8.0 and written approval of the Head of Department. Credit from recognised exchange programmes may be transferred only if the Learning Agreement was approved before departure.
title: Programme Duration and Credit Load

text:
Nexus University uses a ten-point grade point scale. Letter grades and grade points are: O (10), A+ (9), A (8), B+ (7), B (6), C (5), P (4), and F (0). Internal assessment normally contributes forty percent of the course total and the end-semester examination contributes sixty percent, unless the course file approved by the Board of Studies states a studio or laboratory pattern. A student must obtain at least forty percent in the end-semester examination and at least forty percent in the overall course total to earn a pass grade. Relative grading may be used in large first-year courses if announced in the first week. Incomplete grades (I) must be converted within the following semester or they become F.

Grade reports are released through the student portal. Clerical errors may be corrected on application within fifteen days of publication. Requests for re-totaling of end-semester scripts follow the Examination Rules. There is no provision in these Academic Regulations for changing a letter grade on compassionate grounds, nor for awarding a pass by committee vote where the student has not met the published assessment requirements.
title: Grading System

text:
Internal assessment typically comprises a mid-semester test, at least one assignment or laboratory record, and class participation or quizzes, as stated in the course plan. Instructors shall publish the component weights in the first week. Students who miss a mid-semester test without approved leave receive zero for that component. Make-up mid-semester tests are granted only for University duty, approved medical exemption, or bereavement of an immediate family member, and must be completed before the start of end-semester examinations. Assignments submitted after the published deadline lose ten percent of the assignment marks per working day, up to a maximum of five working days, after which the assignment is not accepted.

Group assignments require a contribution statement. If a team member is found not to have contributed, that member may receive a reduced mark without automatically penalising contributing members. Plagiarism in assignments is handled under academic misconduct rules in the Student Discipline policy. Recycling of a student's own previously submitted work without citation is treated as unacknowledged reuse and may attract a mark penalty.
title: Internal Assessment Components

text:
A student remains in good academic standing if the semester grade point average is at least 5.0 and the cumulative grade point average is at least 5.0. A student whose semester grade point average falls below 5.0 is placed on academic warning. Two consecutive warnings result in academic probation. A student on probation must meet the Head of Department, limit extracurricular office-holding, and follow a reduced-credit plan if advised. Failure to raise the cumulative grade point average above 5.0 after two probation semesters may lead to discontinuation from the programme after a hearing before the Faculty Academic Committee.

Progression to the next year of study requires the student to have earned the minimum credits listed in the programme structure, including all listed core courses of the previous year or an approved equivalent. Carrying more than three backlogs into the final year is not permitted except by Dean's waiver after a documented review of remaining degree requirements.
title: Academic Standing and Progression

text:
Every student shall carry the University identity card while on campus and produce it when asked by authorised staff. The card is required to enter the library, hostels, examination halls, and laboratories after hours. Loss of a card must be reported to Student Services within twenty-four hours. A duplicate card is issued on payment of the published replacement fee. Lending an identity card to another person is a disciplinary offence.

The Central Library is open from 8:00 AM to 10:00 PM on teaching days and from 9:00 AM to 5:00 PM on Sundays, except University holidays. Undergraduate students may borrow up to four print volumes for fourteen days. Overdue charges apply as posted at the circulation desk. Food, loud conversation, and unauthorised photography of rare collections are prohibited. Remote access to licensed electronic resources is limited to current members and must not be shared outside the University.
title: Identity Cards, Library, and Campus Access

text: Each department shall maintain a Student Academic Committee with elected student members from each year of study. The committee may recommend improvements to timetables, laboratory access, and academic support, but it cannot alter grading schemes or attendance rules. University-wide student representation occurs through the Nexus Student Council, whose constitution is approved by the Dean of Student Affairs. Office-bearers must remain in good academic standing. Committees shall keep minutes and may not collect unofficial fees.
title: Student Committees and Representation

text: Academic leave of up to five working days in a semester may be granted by the Head of Department for University representation in approved competitions, conferences, or official duty. Leave does not by itself reduce the attendance denominator unless the circular granting leave states that the absence is duty leave. Personal travel, family functions that are not bereavement, and internships that were not pre-approved as credit-bearing do not qualify as academic leave under this section. Medical leave is processed under the Medical Exemption Rules issued as a separate document.
title: Leave from Academic Activities

text: A change of undergraduate branch, where vacancies exist, may be considered only after the first year and only on the basis of first-year cumulative grade point average and availability. Applications close on the date announced by the Dean of Academic Affairs, ordinarily before the start of the third semester. Lateral movement between unrelated postgraduate programmes is not permitted.
title: Branch or Programme Change

text: Doubts about interpretation of these Academic Regulations shall be referred to the Registrar. If two academic documents appear to address the same requirement differently, the matter shall be placed before the Academic Council. Until the Council decides, instructors shall apply the stricter published academic standard for assessment integrity, while students may seek written clarification. Informal oral assurances are not a defence against a published rule.
title: Interpretation

text: Nexus University Attendance Policy
title: 02 Attendance Policy

text: This Attendance Policy explains how class presence is recorded, how shortages are notified, and how attendance relates to examination eligibility. It applies to lectures, tutorials, laboratories, studios, and mandatory workshops that appear on the official timetable. The policy should be read with the Examination Rules and the Medical Exemption Rules.
title: Academic Year 2026-2027

text:
Attendance is marked in the student information system at the start of each scheduled session. For a lecture of fifty minutes, a student who arrives more than ten minutes late may be marked absent at the instructor's discretion, which shall be applied consistently to the whole class. Laboratory attendance requires presence for the full session unless the instructor records an authorised early departure. Proxy attendance, signing for another student, or sharing a login session to falsify presence is academic misconduct.

Biometric or smart-card readers, where installed, are the primary record. If a reader fails, the instructor's signed paper roll, uploaded the same day, is accepted. Students who believe a session was marked incorrectly must raise a correction request within three working days. Requests raised after that period are not entertained except where the system was demonstrably unavailable.
title: Recording of Attendance

text:
Students require at least 75% attendance in each registered course to appear for the semester examination of that course. Attendance is calculated as the number of sessions attended divided by the number of sessions held, multiplied by one hundred, and rounded to two decimal places. The 75% threshold applies to lectures and to laboratories separately where a course has both components with independent session counts. Students below the threshold are notified as having an attendance shortage and are not issued an examination hall ticket for the affected course.

Departments shall compute attendance one week before the start of end-semester examinations and freeze the figure after a two-day correction window. No instructor may privately lower the 75% rule for an individual student. Condonation, if any, follows only the procedures in Section 4.5 of this policy and does not replace the ordinary 75% rule for students without an approved pathway.
title: Attendance Requirements

text: When a student's attendance in a course falls below eighty percent at mid-semester, the Department Office shall send a caution notice to the student portal and to the registered email address. A second notice is sent if attendance falls below seventy-five percent before the freeze date. Failure to read a notice is not an excuse. Mentors shall discuss attendance with students on warning or probation. Parents or guardians listed in the enrolment record may be informed when attendance in two or more courses is below seventy percent.
title: Shortage Notices and Monitoring

text: Students deputed by the University to represent Nexus University in official sports, cultural, or academic events may receive duty leave. Duty leave sessions are excluded from the denominator of the attendance calculation for the dates named in the deputation letter. Informal club travel without a deputation letter does not qualify. The maximum duty-leave exclusion in a semester is ten teaching days unless the Dean of Student Affairs authorises a larger exclusion for national-level representation.
title: University Duty and Representational Absence

text: A student whose attendance is below 75% but not below 70%, and who has no disciplinary probation, may apply for condonation on payment of the condonation fee published for the semester. Condonation is not a right. The Head of Department may refuse condonation where the student has a pattern of unexplained absence. Condonation cannot be combined with an unapproved late medical claim. Students below 70% without an approved medical exemption remain ineligible for the end-semester examination in that course.
title: Condonation of Shortage

text: Practical courses require presence because skills cannot be demonstrated by reading alone. Missing more than the permitted fraction of laboratory sessions may make the student ineligible for the practical examination even if theory attendance is adequate. Make-up laboratory sessions, if offered, are scheduled at the department's convenience and are not guaranteed. Safety briefing attendance is compulsory; a student who misses the briefing may be barred from the laboratory until the briefing is completed.
title: Laboratories, Studios, and Clinical Sessions

text: If a course is approved for hybrid delivery, online presence counts only when the student joins with the registered account, keeps the camera policy of the course, and remains for the required duration. Connection failure is not automatically excused. Students must notify the instructor during the session or immediately after with evidence of an outage. Recorded lectures, where provided as a supplement, do not themselves create attendance credit unless the course plan states a verified viewing requirement.
title: Online and Hybrid Sessions

text: Students with documented disabilities may receive reasonable adjustments to the method of recording attendance, such as a designated seat or assistance with card tap, but the 75% quantitative requirement in Section 4.2 remains the default eligibility rule unless a specific adjustment is written into an approved accessibility plan. Pregnant students and student-parents may request timetable consideration; such requests do not by themselves alter the percentage threshold.
title: Special Categories

text: Instructors shall close attendance within twenty-four hours of a session. They shall not mark a student present as a favour. They shall publish a running attendance view on the portal or an equivalent channel at least twice in the semester before the freeze. Failure of an instructor to mark a session is corrected by the Head of Department using the timetable as evidence that the session was held.
title: Responsibilities of Instructors

text: Disputes about arithmetic shall be resolved from system logs. Disputes about whether a session was held shall be resolved from the official timetable and the instructor's session plan.
title: Interpretation of Attendance Disputes

text: Nexus University Examination Rules
title: 03 Examination Rules

text: These Examination Rules govern eligibility, conduct, evaluation, and results for end-semester and supplementary examinations conducted by Nexus University. The Controller of Examinations is responsible for operational delivery. Academic judgements on content remain with examiners appointed by Boards of Studies.
title: Academic Year 2026-2027

text:
A student may be issued a hall ticket only if the student is registered for the course, has no unpaid examination fee for that session, and meets the attendance requirement applicable to the course under the Attendance Policy. Students barred for attendance shortage, pending disciplinary suspension, or missing identity verification cannot enter the examination hall. Eligibility lists are published at least four working days before the first examination of the session.

Possession of a hall ticket does not override a later discovery of ineligibility caused by fee default or a proven attendance falsification. In such cases the script, if written, may be cancelled.
title: Examination Eligibility

text: Hall tickets are available on the student portal. Students must carry the hall ticket and the University identity card to every session. A temporary identity slip issued on the same day by Student Services may be accepted once in a semester if the identity card is lost and a complaint number is produced. Photograph mismatch or impersonation is referred immediately to the flying squad and to the disciplinary authority.
title: Hall Tickets and Identity

text:
Candidates shall occupy the allotted seat fifteen minutes before the start time. Bags, mobile phones, smart watches, programmable calculators (unless permitted for that paper), notes, and Bluetooth devices are prohibited inside the hall. The invigilator's instruction is binding during the session. Communication between candidates, glancing at another script, or writing after time is called constitutes misconduct. Rough work must be done in the answer book.

A candidate who arrives more than thirty minutes late is not admitted. No candidate may leave the hall during the first thirty minutes or the last fifteen minutes of a written paper. Biological breaks are escorted where the duration of the paper exceeds two hours.

If a candidate becomes ill during a paper, the invigilator shall call medical assistance. The candidate may be allowed to continue or to withdraw. Withdrawal does not by itself create a right to a special examination on another day except where the Medical Exemption Rules and a later decision of the Controller of Examinations jointly authorise a make-up sitting. Question papers are not emailed to candidates.
title: Examination Conduct

text: Copying, possessing unauthorised material, impersonation, leaking a question paper, or using an electronic device to obtain answers is examination malpractice. The invigilator shall seize material, mark the answer book, and submit a report. The Malpractice Committee may impose penalties ranging from cancellation of the paper to cancellation of the semester or rustication, depending on severity and prior record. A student under inquiry may be permitted to write remaining papers provisionally; results remain withheld until the inquiry ends.
title: Academic Misconduct in Examinations

text: Illness arising in the hall is managed as an invigilation incident. Make-up sittings exist only when separately authorised in writing after a medical review. This section does not list social or travel reasons for missing a paper.
title: Medical Situations During an Examination

text: End-semester scripts are evaluated by appointed examiners. Results are published on the portal. A student may apply for re-totaling within ten days of result publication on payment of the prescribed fee. Revaluation of theory scripts, where offered for that programme, follows the same window. Practical and viva marks are not revalued except for documented clerical error. The higher mark after revaluation, if the scheme so provides, replaces the original theory mark.
title: Evaluation, Re-totaling, and Revaluation

text: Supplementary examinations are conducted for courses in which the student earned F or was absent with approved medical exemption. Improvement examinations, if announced, are limited to courses with pass grades and do not extend programme duration automatically. A student cannot use supplementary sittings to bypass an attendance bar from the original semester; the student must re-register and meet eligibility in a later offering unless a specific make-up eligibility has been granted in writing.
title: Supplementary and Improvement Examinations

text: Internal assessment marks are submitted by departments before the start of end-semester examinations. The Controller of Examinations shall not accept revised internals after the deadline except to correct a proven portal error. Students must obtain the minimum end-semester mark stated in the Academic Regulations even if internals are high. Conversely, strong examination performance does not replace a missing laboratory internal where the laboratory is a distinct component.
title: Internal Assessment and Examination Relationship

text: Question papers follow the pattern in the approved course file. Unless the programme is taught in another language, papers are in English. Students may request a large-print paper or additional time only under an approved accessibility plan filed with the Controller of Examinations at least three weeks before the session.
title: Question Papers and Language

text: Official transcripts are issued by the Registrar. Degree certificates are conferred at Convocation or collected afterwards according to the Registrar's collection notice. Replacement of a damaged certificate follows the process published by the Registrar's office.
title: Degree Certificates and Transcripts

text: The University may deploy a flying squad and closed-circuit cameras in examination buildings. Recordings are used only for integrity inquiries and are retained for the period stated in the data-protection notice. Tampering with cameras or obstructing a squad member is a separate offence.
title: Flying Squad and Surveillance

text: The Controller of Examinations interprets operational examination questions. Academic content disputes go to the Board of Studies. These rules do not create examination centres outside the campus except for approved distance-proctored courses that the Academic Council has specifically listed.
title: Interpretation

text: Nexus University Fee Policy
title: 04 Fee Policy

text: This Fee Policy states tuition, examination, hostel, and related charges, and the University's rules on payment, late fees, and refunds. Amounts may be revised by the Finance Committee; the figures below are those notified for Academic Year 2026-2027 unless a later official circular supersedes them. Payments are accepted by the methods listed in Section 9.4.
title: Academic Year 2026-2027

text:
Undergraduate tuition for regular engineering and science programmes is payable each semester as billed on the student portal. Postgraduate tuition follows the offer letter. Scholarships, if awarded, are adjustments to the billed amount and do not themselves create a right to delay payment of the residual dues. A student who has not paid tuition is not in good financial standing and may be denied course registration, examination hall tickets, and hostel occupancy.

The University does not reduce tuition because a student attends fewer electives than the maximum load. Tuition is a programme semester charge, not a per-credit invoice, except for approved part-time postgraduate schemes that are billed per credit in the offer letter.
title: Tuition and Programme Fees

text: In addition to tuition, students pay an examination fee per registered end-semester session, a library and information resources fee, a student activity fee, and, where applicable, laboratory consumable charges notified by the department. Identity-card replacement, condonation, re-totaling, and duplicate transcript fees are published in the portal fee catalogue. Unofficial collections by student clubs cannot be billed as University fees.
title: Other Mandatory Charges

text:
For Academic Year 2026-2027, undergraduate tuition for the Odd Semester is due on 15 August 2026. This deadline applies to all continuing undergraduate students in regular programmes. New first-year students follow the date printed on the admission offer, which shall not be later than the date of commencement of instruction. Even Semester undergraduate tuition is due on 10 January 2027. Examination fees for each session are due not later than seven days before the first paper of that session.

Hostel rent, where the student is an alloted resident, is due on the same date as tuition for that semester unless the Hostel Office issues a separate instalment plan in writing. Late payment attracts the late fee in Section 9.5. Students waiting for a sanctioned education loan must upload the loan-sanction letter before the due date to request a short administrative extension; an extension is not automatic.
title: Payment Deadlines

text: Fees shall be paid through the University payment gateway using net banking, debit card, credit card, or Unified Payments Interface, or by demand draft drawn in favour of Nexus University as specified on the portal. Cash is not accepted at departmental offices. A payment is complete only when the portal shows a success receipt with a University transaction identifier.
title: Permitted Payment Methods

text: A late fee of two percent of the overdue tuition component accrues for the first week after the deadline, and an additional one percent may accrue for each subsequent week up to a published cap. After four weeks of default without an approved extension, the University may debar the student from classes and examinations until dues are cleared. Partial payments are credited first to the oldest tuition component.
title: Late Fees and Debarment

text: A student who withdraws before the commencement of instruction may receive a refund of tuition after deduction of the processing amount stated in the admission brochure. After instruction begins, refunds follow a sliding scale published by the Finance Office and do not include non-refundable registration charges. Hostel refunds depend on occupancy and notice. Scholarship amounts already credited may be recovered if the student becomes ineligible.
title: Refunds and Withdrawal

text: Fee concession is distinct from scholarship. Concession on humanitarian grounds, if any, is decided by a committee chaired by the Registrar and is documented. Staff-ward concessions follow a separate ordinance. No teacher or warden may privately waive a fee.
title: Fee Concessions

text: Students shall retain electronic receipts. Disputes about payment must be raised within thirty days with bank evidence. The University is not responsible for payments made to unofficial accounts advertised on messaging groups.
title: Records and Receipts

text: Financial standing does not replace academic eligibility. A student who has paid fees but has an attendance shortage remains ineligible under the Attendance Policy. A student who has academic eligibility but unpaid examination fees remains ineligible under the Examination Rules. The fee deadline in Section 9.3 is the rule applied by the Finance Office for Odd Semester undergraduate tuition unless a later Finance Committee circular expressly replaces that date.
title: Relationship to Other Policies

text: Nexus University Hostel Handbook
title: 05 Hostel Handbook

text: This Hostel Handbook governs residence in University hostels on the main campus. Occupation of a room is a licence, not a tenancy. Residents remain subject to the Student Discipline Code and to campus safety directions issued by the Chief Warden.
title: Academic Year 2026-2027

text:
Hostel gates close according to the published in-time. On weekdays, the hostel curfew is 10:00 PM. Residents must be inside their allotted hostel by 10:00 PM Sunday through Thursday. After curfew, entry is recorded as late entry. Repeated late entry without prior permission from the warden may lead to a written warning, informing of parents or guardians, and, after three recorded late entries in a semester, referral to the Hostel Disciplinary Committee.

Night roll is taken after curfew. A resident who is absent without leave is treated as missing for safety purposes and the warden may notify campus security. The weekday curfew of 10:00 PM applies during teaching weeks, mid-semester tests, and end-semester examinations unless the Chief Warden posts a special circular for a named event.
title: Weekday Curfew and Entry

text: On Fridays and Saturdays, and on nights before a declared University holiday, in-time is 11:00 PM unless a more restrictive circular is issued during a security alert. Weekend hours do not authorise overnight absence from the city. Residents who wish to leave campus overnight must file a leave application.
title: Weekend and Holiday Hours

text: Leave of one night or more requires an online application approved by the warden. For residents below eighteen years of age, parent confirmation is required. Leave to stay with local relatives is not automatic; an address and contact number are mandatory. Guest rooms, if any, are booked through the Hostel Office for limited visiting hours only.
title: Leave from Hostel

text: Rooms are allotted by the Hostel Office. Unauthorised room changes, extra furniture, cooking coils, and high-load appliances are prohibited. Residents are jointly responsible for common-area damage on their floor if individual responsibility cannot be established. Lights and fans shall be switched off when leaving. Quiet hours begin at 11:00 PM in corridors even when weekend in-time is later.
title: Rooms, Inventory, and Energy

text: Day visitors may be received in the designated lobby between 4:00 PM and 7:00 PM after entry in the visitor register. Visitors are not permitted in residential corridors of another gender's hostel. Delivery personnel shall leave parcels at the gate office.
title: Visitors

text: Mess membership follows the hostel allotment. Temporary mess-off requires application three working days in advance and is limited to the days published by the mess committee. Wasting food, entering the kitchen without authorisation, and removing utensils is prohibited. Ill residents should inform the warden so that a sick-diet arrangement can be considered; this is not a medical exemption from academic rules.
title: Mess and Hygiene

text: Possession or use of tobacco, alcohol, or illegal substances in hostels is a serious offence. Ragging in any form is prohibited and is reported under national anti-ragging regulations as well as University discipline. Fire equipment shall not be tampered with. Parking of two-wheelers is allowed only in marked bays. Security staff directions at the gate are binding.
title: Safety, Substances, and Conduct

text: Residents vacate within twenty-four hours after the last examination of the even semester unless summer stay is sanctioned for internship or supplementary examinations. Personal property left behind may be stored for thirty days and then disposed of. Room inspection deductions are taken from the hostel deposit.
title: Vacating and Summer Stay

text: Maintenance complaints are lodged on the hostel portal. Harassment complaints may be made to the warden, the Chief Warden, or the Internal Complaints Committee as applicable. Retaliation against a complainant is an independent offence.
title: Complaints

text: Hostel in-time is a residence rule. Campus-wide conduct rules appear in the Student Discipline policy. Residents must follow both. Where a safety emergency exists, the Chief Warden may lock gates earlier than the ordinary curfew and shall record the reason.
title: Relationship to Campus Discipline

text: Nexus University Student Discipline Code
title: 06 Student Discipline

text: This Student Discipline Code states expected conduct on campus, in hostels, online University forums, and University-sponsored off-campus events. It also describes inquiries and penalties. Academic evaluation remains governed by the Academic Regulations and Examination Rules; this Code addresses behaviour.
title: Academic Year 2026-2027

text: Students shall treat staff, visitors, and fellow students with respect. Intimidation, hate speech, harassment, and discrimination on prohibited grounds are offences. Students shall comply with lawful directions of University officials during emergencies. Posting confidential examination material or another student's private data on public platforms is misconduct.
title: General Conduct

text: Students shall not lend identity cards, tailgate through access gates, or enter restricted laboratories without authorisation. Theft, vandalism, and unauthorised use of University computing resources are offences. Lost property should be deposited with campus security.
title: Identity, Access, and Property

text: Plagiarism, collusion, fabrication of data, and unauthorized contract cheating in assignments are academic misconduct even when they occur outside an examination hall. Instructors shall report suspected cases to the Head of Department. Penalties may include zero for the assessment, failure in the course, and a disciplinary annotation. Repeated offences may lead to suspension.
title: Academic Integrity Outside the Hall

text: Ragging is prohibited. Sexual harassment complaints follow the University policy implementing applicable law. Students must not possess weapons. Drone flying over hostels or examination buildings without authorisation is prohibited.
title: Ragging, Harassment, and Safety

text: The campus is tobacco-free in academic buildings. Alcohol is not permitted in hostels or undergraduate events. Controlled substances are prohibited. Being intoxicated on campus and unable to take safety directions is an offence even if consumption occurred off campus.
title: Alcohol, Tobacco, and Controlled Substances

text:
Resident students are required to return to their hostels by 11:00 PM on weekdays. This campus conduct rule is intended to reduce late-night risk on internal roads and to support a consistent security deployment at hostel gates. Security officers may stop a resident student on campus after 11:00 PM on a weekday and record the student as being outside hostel in-time. The 11:00 PM weekday return obligation applies during teaching weeks. Special late permissions, if granted for a University event, must be carried in writing.

Resident students found repeatedly on campus after 11:00 PM on weekdays without permission may be fined and referred to the Student Disciplinary Committee. This section is a binding conduct requirement for hostel residents and is used by campus security in incident reports.
title: Campus Return Hours for Resident Students

text: Peaceful assembly in designated areas is allowed with prior intimation to the Dean of Student Affairs when more than fifty participants are expected. Blocking gates, occupying offices, and using amplification after 9:00 PM near hostels is not permitted. Political campaigning by external parties on campus requires Registrar approval.
title: Demonstrations and Public Expression

text: University email and learning platforms are official channels. Impersonating staff online, sharing login credentials, and conducting cyberbullying against members of the University community are offences. Students should not assume that deleted messages are untraceable on University systems.
title: Digital Conduct

text: A show-cause notice shall state the alleged facts. The student may submit a written defence and may be heard in person. Penalties include warning, fine, community restitution, withdrawal of facilities, suspension, and rustication. Interim suspension may be used where safety is at risk. Appeals lie to the Vice-Chancellor's nominee within fifteen days.
title: Inquiries and Penalties

text: The Student Disciplinary Committee includes faculty members and, except in cases of sexual harassment or ragging where separate statutory committees apply, may include a student representative who is not connected to the incident. The committee shall record reasons. This Code does not authorise student committees to impose unofficial punishments.
title: Committees

text: Hostel residents must also follow the Hostel Handbook. Security incident reports may cite this Code, the handbook, or both. Students seeking clarification of night hours should read Section 15.6 together with hostel entry rules and, if the texts appear difficult to reconcile, request written guidance from the Dean of Student Affairs.
title: Relationship to Hostel Rules

text: Nexus University Scholarship Policy
title: 07 Scholarship Policy

text: This Scholarship Policy describes merit, need-linked, and special awards administered by Nexus University for Academic Year 2026-2027. External government scholarships follow the rules of the awarding body; the University only facilitates verification.
title: Academic Year 2026-2027

text: The University administers (a) Merit Scholarships based on prior academic performance, (b) Need-Linked Tuition Support based on documented family income, (c) Sports and Cultural Awards for University representation at specified levels, and (d) Donor Awards bound by gift agreements. A student may hold more than one award only if the combined tuition waiver does not exceed one hundred percent of billed tuition and the donor agreement allows stacking.
title: Categories of Award

text: Continuing undergraduate Merit Scholarships require a cumulative grade point average of at least 8.5 and no F grade in the review period, together with good disciplinary standing. First-year entry merit awards follow the admission rank lists published by the Admissions Office. Merit awards are reviewed every even semester. A fall in cumulative grade point average below 8.0 leads to discontinuation of the merit award from the following semester.
title: Merit Scholarship Criteria

text: Need-linked support requires income documents specified in the annual circular, typically including a recent income certificate and bank statements. False disclosure is disciplinary misconduct and leads to recovery of funds. Need-linked support does not waive hostel mess charges unless the award letter says so. Deadlines for need-linked applications are announced on the portal; late applications are not considered except where the circular allows a documented portal outage.
title: Need-Linked Support

text: Awards require a recommendation from the Director of Physical Education or the Cultural Coordinator and evidence of representation. Doping violations or match-fixing allegations under inquiry suspend the award. These awards do not create attendance waivers beyond duty leave granted under the Attendance Policy.
title: Sports and Cultural Awards

text: Donor awards may include additional essay, interview, or service conditions. The University will not alter academic grading to satisfy a donor. If a donor condition conflicts with University non-discrimination policy, the University condition prevails and the award may be declined.
title: Donor Awards

text: Awards may be withdrawn for academic misconduct, ragging findings, or fee default that is not cured. Some professional programme awards include a service bond as stated in the award letter. This policy does not authorise conversion of a scholarship into cash for personal travel, nor payment of the award to a third party.
title: Continuation, Withdrawal, and Bond

text: Students apply on the scholarship portal. Decisions are communicated by email. Appeals on procedure, not on academic judgement of merit rank, may be filed within ten days to the Dean of Academic Affairs. There is no walk-in allotment of donor seats in departmental offices.
title: Application and Appeals

text: Scholarship disbursement is ordinarily an internal credit against tuition. Until the credit appears, the student should follow Fee Policy deadlines or request a documented bridging note from the Scholarship Cell. A bridging note is not available merely because an application is pending.
title: Interaction with Fees

text: The Scholarship Cell retains applications for the period required by audit rules. Students should keep copies. This policy does not create a scholarship for every student with a high grade; awards are limited by budget.

Nexus University | Academic Year 2026-2027
Medical Exemption Rules (Office of the Registrar)
title: Medical Exemption

text:
Nexus University recognises that serious illness or injury may prevent a student from meeting ordinary
academic attendance expectations. These Medical Exemption Rules apply for Academic Year 2026-2027. An
exemption is not automatic. The student must apply, attach supporting evidence, and wait for written approval
from the Medical Review Committee acting with the Office of the Registrar.
title: Purpose of Medical Exemption

text:
Eligible circumstances include hospitalisation of more than forty-eight hours, communicable disease requiring
isolation on medical advice, scheduled surgery with a recovery period certified by a registered medical
practitioner, and acute psychiatric crisis treated by the University Health Centre or an equivalent licensed
facility. Seasonal cold, routine outpatient visits, and undocumented fatigue are not eligible. Travel for rest is
not a medical ground.
title: Eligible Medical Circumstances

text:
The student shall submit Form MX-26 within seven calendar days of returning to academic activity, or earlier
if the absence is foreseeable. The form must include diagnosis category, period of incapacity, treating
practitioner registration number, and a statement of academic impact. Delayed applications may be accepted
only where the student was medically incapable of filing on time, as certified in writing.
title: Application Procedure

text:
Where a student has received an approved medical exemption covering the relevant teaching period, the
student may be permitted to appear for the semester examination if the student has maintained at least 60%
attendance in that course, counted after excluding days covered by the approved exemption. This medical
pathway is intended to prevent unfair exclusion of students who were hospitalised or otherwise certified unfit.
Coursework still due must be completed under a make-up schedule issued by the course instructor and
recorded by the Department Office.
title: Examination Eligibility After Approved Medical Exemption

text:
The University may verify certificates with the issuing hospital or clinic. Forged, altered, or purchased medical
documents constitute academic misconduct under the Student Discipline Code and may lead to cancellation
of the exemption, failure in the course, and disciplinary probation. Students must keep original documents for
one year after the decision.
title: Supporting Documents and Verification

text:
A medical exemption does not waive tuition, hostel rent, or examination fees. It does not authorise absence
from a university inquiry, does not extend the maximum duration of the programme, and does not create a
right to a special examination date except as separately provided in the Examination Rules. Repeat medical
exemptions in consecutive semesters are reviewed with heightened scrutiny.
title: Limits of Exemption

text:
After approval, the Registrar shall notify the Head of Department, the course instructors concerned, and the
Controller of Examinations. Instructors shall not reduce internal assessment solely because medically
exempted hours were missed, provided the student completes an equivalent academic task when reasonably
possible.

title: Notification to Departments

text:
A student may appeal a refused medical exemption to the Dean of Student Affairs within ten working days.
The appeal board shall include one faculty member from outside the student's department and one medical
adviser who was not the original reviewer. The appeal decision is final for that semester.
